To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cloud feedback is negative, i.e., an increase in cloudiness reduces net radiation, but the magnitude of this feedback is relatively small compared to the albedo effect, which increases net radiation.

(a) the cloudiness feedback is likely to be important for the surface energy balance of rainforests, and (b) this feedback is likely to reduce net surface radiation, and hence to reduce the magnitude of the surface warming due to large-scale deforestation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of land cover changes on the surface energy budget of the Amazon forest.
the role of clouds in modifying the surface energy balance of a tropical rainforest, in particular the Amazon forest.
the impact of deforestation on surface energy and water balances in the humid tropics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the net effect of clouds on the surface energy fluxes is to reduce the net radiation at the surface; this effect is more pronounced on the terrestrial radiation than on the solar radiation; and the net effect of a 1% change in cloudiness on the surface energy budget is ca. -1 W/m 2.
the net effect of deforestation on the radiation balance is likely to have only a minor effect, but the effect on terrestrial radiation may be more significant than the effect on solar radiation.

the role of clouds in modifying the radiation field at the surface is to reduce net solar radiation, and to increase net terrestrial radiation, both of which will tend to reduce the surface energy balance, and hence the surface temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deforestation of the tropical rainforests will have a significant impact on the surface energy fluxes.

the net effect of clouds on the energy balance is to reduce the net radiation, and the net effect of deforestation on clouds is to decrease the cloudiness, which in turn reduces the net radiation, but the net effect of this is to increase net radiation.
the role of cloudiness in the surface energy budget is to reduce the net radiation at the land surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the net effect of clouds on net radiation is negative.

the effect of deforestation on the Amazon forest is to reduce net solar radiation, and this reduction is of the same order of magnitude as the effect of deforested surface albedo on net solar radiation.
the effect of deforestation on the energy budget over Amazonia is likely to be dominated by the change in terrestrial radiation, not by the change in solar radiation.
